# Why now

> If I tick this, am I confirming every figure in the table? And if one turns out wrong, can I take it back?
> — A colleague from SEO, with the publication open in front of them

Every required step is done, and the window reads the whole card back: the texts written with Claude and those a colleague wrote before. Above the card, the window says who will see the Resource once it is published. At the bottom is one sentence to tick, "For SEO, I have read this card and confirm that this Resource is correct: what it is and what it stands for, in every text on it.", with the button that publishes next to it, off until the sentence is ticked.

Promise: what you declare when you publish a Resource, who sees it then, and why there is no way back.

# Core idea

Publishing a Resource is its first **Confirmation**: you declare for your Owner Unit that every text on its card is right about what the Resource is and what it stands for, not about its figures, and from then on everyone who sees its Collection sees it, as a Publication is not undone.

## At Immoscoop

A colleague of SEO opens the publication of Search Console impressions, whole site. It says who will see it: everyone who sees Attraction, which is the whole company as the Collection is public, where now only SEO and the Data Team do. It reads the card back: the Business Description next to the description from dbt, the intended use, the pitfalls, the Known Gap with the day it is reliable since, and the Key Fields. The pitfall about the average position was written by someone else before the Owner Journey, and the declaration covers it as well. The colleague reads every text, ticks the declaration and presses Publish and confirm themselves, in the window Claude shows or in Data Hub itself; Claude never presses it. The Level rises from 2 · Described to 3 · Confirmed, and Data Hub keeps the declaration, in the words that were ticked, with the Confirmation. The Confirmation vouches for what the Resource is; its figures are for the EDA to explore. Should SEO later want nobody to build on it any more, they mark it deprecated: the Publication stays.

# Check your understanding

## You publish a Resource in a Collection that is private. Who sees it from then on?

- [ ] The whole company: publishing shows a Resource to everyone
- [ ] Only the colleagues who asked for it
- [x] Everyone who sees the Collection: for a private one, still only your Owner Unit and the Data Team, until the Collection is made public

Why: a Publication shows a Resource to the readers of its Collection, no further. The publication says who will see it before you tick anything.

## A month after you published a Resource, your team would rather nobody built on it any more. What do you do?

- [ ] Unpublish it, so that only your team sees it again
- [ ] Ask the Data Team to unpublish it for you
- [x] Mark it deprecated, with why and what to use instead: the Resource stays published

Why: a Publication is not undone, so whoever built on the Resource keeps it. Deprecated discourages its use and says what to use instead, without hiding or blocking anything.

## Claude drafted most texts on your card with you, and a colleague wrote the pitfalls before you started. What does your declaration vouch for?

- [ ] Only the texts you typed yourself
- [ ] The texts you agreed to with Claude; the pitfalls stay your colleague's
- [x] Every text on the card, whoever wrote it first: that is why the window reads the whole card back

Why: the declaration accepts every text on the card, also those written before, by a colleague or in an earlier conversation, and Data Hub keeps it in the words you ticked. A text you do not stand for yet goes back to its step before you tick.

# You can now

read the whole card back before you publish a Resource, and ask "do I stand for every text on it, also those I did not write?" before you tick the declaration.
